uncited: The Field Error Metric quantifies the approximation quality of a simplified mesh by measuring the discrepancy in scalar field values between the original and simplified representations.
It solves the problem of evaluating volumetric fidelity where surface-only metrics fail to capture internal data variations.

Unlike its parent [Mean-Square Error Metric for Scalar Fields](7137-mean-square-error-metric-for-scalar-fields.md), which sums squared differences within tetrahedra, this method samples the domain and explicitly ignores points outside the simplified mesh's domain, treating them as surface boundary errors instead.
Original scalar field defined on a domain (typically a tetrahedral mesh).
Scalar field range $R = \max(f) - \min(f)$ of the original field.
- Sample points $P$: A set of 3D coordinates.
This includes original mesh vertices and interpolated points inside tetrahedra.
- Scalar values $f(p)$: The field value at point $p$.
**Sampling:** Generate sample points $P$ within the domain of the original mesh.
**Filtering:** Discard any point $p$ that lies outside the simplified mesh domain.
Let $P_{valid}$ be the set of sample points inside the simplified mesh domain.
The parent article uses squared differences.
We assume absolute difference for general "difference" unless squared is specified, but given the parent is MSE, the implementation may vary.
- **Interpolation accuracy:** The quality of $f_{simp}(p)$ depends on the interpolation method used within the simplified mesh elements.
- **Time Complexity:** Depends on the number of sample points and the cost of evaluating the simplified mesh field and checking domain inclusion.
- **Memory Complexity:** Requires storage for sample points and field values.
Sensitive to the definition of "inside" for the simplified mesh.
- **When to use:** When volumetric data fidelity is critical and surface approximation is insufficient.
- **When not to use:** When only surface geometry matters or when computational resources are limited.
It was proposed as an alternative to surface boundary error measurement (using Metro [30]) to evaluate the quality of simplified field data.
The method is similar to approaches by Cignoni et al. [11] but differs by ignoring points outside the simplified mesh domain to separate field error from surface error.
